instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Not Why We Drifted
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation away from the real reason the relationship changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've got our afternoon arranged: same picnic, same sandwiches, and we'll take the spot under that tree.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The last time we came here, you said we needed space. Why?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll have plenty under the tree. I'll carry everything; you can choose sun or shade.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Moving the blanket won't stop me asking why.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll stay here. I'll unpack, and you tell me whether the mustard's finally right. You always had the deciding vote on that. We'll get the sandwiches settled first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I've found our wedding video. Shall we watch it? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather discuss why we're living separately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Here's your father's speech. We never could agree what he meant by 'good luck'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He meant exactly this. Pause it. I don't want another speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Paused. Let's skip to the dancing, then. No speeches. You can help me settle whether your uncle actually falls into the cake.

cards.title: Keep the Peace
cards.instruction: Hide a truth because you believe the relationship cannot survive one more conflict.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Breakfast first; I've got today under control. Leave that letter under my plate. We only just started eating together again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Has your brother cancelled paying us back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The rent is covered; I put my own money in. I'll make fresh toast, however you like it. We don't need another suitcase in the hall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then let me open the letter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After breakfast. You choose how long we sit; I'll clear everything. Yesterday you finally unpacked. Let me keep this morning together before we put another thing between us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle the missing savings. It's a banking complication. You keep our anniversary reservation; I'll have everything in order by Friday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you lend your sister money again?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The money's coming back. We can choose somewhere cheaper tonight if you'd rather. Last time we argued about her, you wanted separate bedrooms.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ring the bank, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the calls to me. You choose the restaurant, and I'll fit the booking around you. We can have a perfectly ordinary anniversary. I need us still sharing a table when Friday comes.

cards.title: Say You Missed Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to admit longing, jealousy, hurt, or attachment before you reveal your own.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm back, so we'll clear up the important bit first: was the flat too quiet without me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you tell me whether you missed me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. One answer each, yours first. You can keep it short: did you ever hear a key and hope it was mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Every evening. There, your turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I rang the landline just to hear you say hello. Right, that's both answers. You can choose what we talk about next; I'll make the tea. Just say hello once more before we move on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll help finish the furniture sale. Sofa goes, but before we decide about my chair, tell me why you've kept it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody offered anything. Did you bring its cushion back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've brought it. I'll do the lifting; you only need to decide this: if someone offered twenty pounds, would you keep the chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I like pretending you're about to sit down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll admit I sleep with the cushion. Chair stays; I'll take its sticker off, if that's all right. You decide where it goes. Could we put the cushion back while I'm sitting in it?

cards.title: We Needed the Break
cards.instruction: Frame a rupture, absence, or failed connection as a healthy decision that ultimately helped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll arrange coffee for Sunday. That year apart did us good; we're ready to manage this properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You used to insist we spend every Saturday together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. We needed the break to stop making free afternoons prove anything. You choose the cafe; I'll come to you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked pottery this Sunday too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Monday, then, or whichever day is free. I'll keep the arrangement simple. Look at what that year taught us: I can organize a coffee without organizing the rest of your weekend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've arranged lunch for just us. That disastrous family reunion did us a favour; we'll put what we learned to work today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We shouted over each other until everyone left.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. An audience made us compete. You can start today, and I'll order while you settle in. Nobody has to win the table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The waiter asked if we're expecting twelve more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell him two. I'll explain the change, and you can keep your turn. That reunion taught us to make room for each other before anybody has to storm out.

cards.title: I Know How to Fix Us
cards.instruction: Perform confidence about repairing the relationship while improvising every step.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. We can fix last night's shouting. Tea first, then one honest sentence each. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want tea. I want you to listen without interrupting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Of course. Listening stage. I'll write down anything I want to interrupt with.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll be writing instead of listening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you keep the pen. Supervised listening. If I interrupt, write it down; we'll start with that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're on stage two of reconciliation. Choose a biscuit; I'll guide us through this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What was stage one?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Getting you to ask about the process. We can spend longer there if you need; I'll answer your questions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't got a process. I want you to stop deciding everything for both of us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Joint planning stage. Exactly. You choose what we talk about first, and I'll keep the biscuits coming. We're already moving forward; I just needed you to tell me which way.
